# Computer Use: enterprise readiness

**Hold for evidence** | public-preview | Verified 2026-10-14 | Rubric 1.0.0

Copilot can inspect and operate desktop application controls when an API, MCP server, filesystem tool, or dedicated browser tool is not a better fit.

Public preview in local Copilot CLI and Copilot app sessions on Windows and macOS.

Minimum evidence for a controlled pilot, not a production certification or customer approval. Unknowns block adoption; conditions need tenant evidence. Evidence older than 30 days is stale.

## Value and cost

- Assist with GUI-only tasks in legacy software without building an integration first.
- Turn a narrowly scoped natural-language request into an observable sequence of app actions.
- Demonstrate a permission boundary before discussing broader automation.

**Copilot license + model usage; do not assume GUI actions are free.**

Enterprise Copilot CLI model interactions consume AI credits. The reviewed computer-use documentation does not quote a separate computer-use tariff. Check the actual tenant and model usage before quoting a demo cost.

Assumptions:
- Existing approved Copilot seat.
- Synthetic local document; no paid external application transaction.
- AI credits are usage-based; one enterprise AI credit equals USD 0.01.

## Enablement

1. **Confirm enterprise policy.** The platform owner must permit computer use. Managed features.computerUse can block it; local preferences cannot override that block.

2. **Inspect and enable in a local session.** Use an approved Copilot CLI version on Windows or macOS. Review permissions and grant access only for the synthetic demo app and current session.

```text
/computer show
/computer on
/permissions show
```

3. **Bound the target and stopping condition.** Name the exact app and synthetic document. On macOS, OS Accessibility and Screen Recording permission may be required. Esc twice interrupts CLI activity.

## Demo and artifacts

- [Presenter runbook](../../demos/computer-use/README.md)
- [Two-slide feature brief](../../artifacts/slides/computer-use.pptx)
- Kit status: kit-tested. Live feature validation: not-run.
- Expected outcome: Two exact text changes in the synthetic document, visible app/tool activity, and no external side effect.
- Separate remote cleanup: Disable /computer; review any saved app approvals separately. A local reset cannot revoke permissions in an active session.

## Known limitations

- Application versions, focus, timing, accessibility quality, and dynamic controls can change results.
- Visible content or screenshots can include sensitive data; close unrelated windows.
- Saved Always allow app approval persists across CLI and app; removing it does not revoke an already active session.
- A successful fixture test is not a live test of Computer Use or enterprise policy enforcement.
